title: Finance & Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition (2026)
author: Eleanor Park
body:
Summary

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard processes for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, contract lifecycle management, procurement approvals and vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition / billing policies for hosted, dedicated, and private products. It is intended as the single source of operational truth for Finance, Legal, Procurement, Product, Sales, and Engineering partners.

Scope and intent
- Audience: Finance, Legal, Procurement, Sales ops, Product managers, Engineering managers.
- Scope: Corporate budgeting and forecasting cycles; contract review and signature workflow; procurement thresholds and PO process; revenue recognition and billing for usage-based, subscription and committed-capacity products.
- Goal: Reduce cycle time, ensure compliant controls, and enable predictable GAAP-compliant revenue recognition.

1) Budgeting and Forecasting cadence

Overview
- Annual operating budget (AOB) prepared by Finance with inputs from all functional leads. AOB aligns to company OKRs, headcount plan, and capital commitments (Dedicated capacity / Private deployment investments).
- Rolling 12-month forecast (R12) updated monthly; re-forecast (re-forecasting major changes) quarterly or on material events (e.g., >10% variance to plan).

Timeline (example calendar year)
1. July–August: Strategic planning and preliminary topline assumptions (revenue targets by product line: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
2. September: Budget packet templates issued to owners (expense templates, headcount, capex requests).
3. October: Manager submissions due. Finance consolidates and runs variance analysis.
4. November: Leadership review and trade-off sessions. Final formal budget signed by CFO and CEO by first business week of December.
5. January: Budget published and uploaded to planning system.
6. Monthly: Rolling forecast refresh due 3rd business day of each month.

Inputs and ownership
- Revenue owners: Sales & GTM (ACV, committed capacity contracts, expected consumption for hosted). Provide pipe-to-forecast mapping and topline assumptions.
- Cost of goods sold (COGS): Eng infra & SRE (GPU fleet costs, cloud egress), Product (hosting).
- Operating expenses: People ops (hiring plan), Eng (contracts for SW licenses, cloud), Sales & Marketing (campaigns).
- Capital requests: Eng-private-deployments team for on-prem packaging and hardware purchases.

Required attachments on submissions
- Business case (one paragraph + expected ROI).
- Owner and approver (manager-level and director-level).
- Related contracts (if a procurement or vendor commitment).

Approval thresholds and delegation
- Up to $25k CAPEX/OPEX: Manager approval.
- $25k–$250k: Director + Finance manager.
- $250k–$1M: VP of the function + FP&A lead.
- >$1M: CFO approval and exec leadership review.

2) Contracts and legal process (contract lifecycle)

Purpose
- Standardize contract review time, ensure appropriate risk and indemnity terms, and clearly define revenue / billing terms for each product line.

Contract types and templates
- Standard SaaS (Hosted API) master services agreement (MSA) + order form.
- Dedicated capacity agreement (includes capacity SLA, reserved pricing, on-call responsibilities).
- Private deployment agreement (includes installation statement of work, on-prem licensing, support SLAs, KMS/HSM requirements).
- NDA (mutual) template.
- Statement of Work (SOW) and change order templates.

Lifecycle steps (typical timeline targets)
1. Request: Sales/partner submits a contract request via Contract Request form (ServiceNow/Jira). Target: same day acknowledgement.
2. Template selection & pre-population: Sales ops selects appropriate template and populates commercial terms (5 business days).
3. Legal review: Legal performs risk assessment and red-lines. Target initial review: 3–5 business days for standard deals; 7–10 business days for complex or multinational agreements.
4. Negotiation: Owner-led negotiation with Legal support. Escalation to GC for non-standard indemnities, export-control clauses, or >$1M liability.
5. Signature: E-sign via DocuSign. Counterparty signature requirements must be validated.
6. Post-signature intake: Contracts team enters executed contract into CLM (contract lifecycle management system) and notifies Finance for revenue recognition setup and Procurement for vendor onboarding (if applicable). Target: 2 business days post-signature.

Contract risk matrix highlights
- Data residency or PII processing: Escalate to Security & Compliance.
- Export-controlled models or cryptographic hardware: Escalate to Legal + Eng-private-deployments.
- Indemnity / liability caps: Standard cap = contract value or 12 months of fees (whichever is greater); deviations require GC approval.
- IP assignment or developer work-for-hire clauses: Legal must review.

3) Procurement procedures and vendor onboarding

Objective
- Centralize vendor procurement, make vendor relationships auditable, and ensure appropriate cost controls for hardware, cloud commitments, and software licenses.

Vendor classification
- Strategic vendor: >$250k/year or mission-critical (e.g., GPU vendor, core infra providers). Requires vendor due diligence and Security questionnaire.
- Standard vendor: $25k–$250k/year. Requires basic procurement form and PO.
- Low-value vendor: < $25k/year. Manager-level purchase with post-hoc PO reconciliation.

Procurement steps
1. Requirement definition: Requestor creates Procurement Request in purchasing system with justification, budget code, and business owner.
2. Approval routing: System routes based on amount to required approvers (see approval thresholds above).
3. Vendor due diligence: For strategic vendors, Procurement + Security run vendor risk assessment (security questionnaire, SOC reports).
4. PO creation and issuance: Procurement issues PO to vendor. No work should commence without an approved PO unless pre-authorized.
5. Receipt and reconciliation: Receipts routed to AP for invoice matching and payment.

Payment terms and preferred methods
- Standard payment terms: Net 30. Deviations must be approved by Finance (treasury).
- Preferred payment: ACH or wire. Corporate cards for low-value subscriptions with pre-approved vendors.

4) Revenue recognition and billing policies

Principles
- Recognize revenue in accordance with ASC 606 (or local GAAP equivalent for non-US entities). Recognize when a performance obligation is satisfied and revenue is reliably measurable.
- Distinguish between product lines for recognition patterns: hosted consumption, committed capacity (Dedicated), and professional services (Private deployments / SOWs).

Product line guidance
- Hosted API (usage-based): Revenue recognized ratably over the period in which tokens/embedding units are consumed. For prepaid credits, recognize as deferred revenue and amortize as consumption occurs.
- Subscriptions (e.g., Console licensing, support add-ons): Recognize ratably over the subscription term.
- Dedicated (committed capacity): Recognize monthly or quarterly ratably over the service period, taking into account any upfront discounts or credits that should be allocated to the service period.
- Private deployments & Professional Services (SOW): Recognize based on transfer of control. For time-and-materials (T&M) SOWs, recognize as services are performed. For fixed-price SOWs, use percentage-of-completion (POC) or milestone basis if POC is reliable and measurable; otherwise defer until completion.

Billing policies and cadence
- Standard billing cadence: Monthly invoicing for usage and subscriptions. Exceptions: annual prepay contracts (invoice at execution) or custom cadence negotiated in the contract.
- Invoicing mechanics: Finance issues invoices via billing system (Stripe/Zuora/ERP). Each invoice must reference executed contract/order form and include line-level breakdown (product, quantity, period, unit price, discounts).
- Credit memos and refunds: Handled by Finance with Sales approval and recorded against revenue in the same period as the credit is issued.

Deferred revenue and contract liabilities
- All prepayments and billed but unearned amounts go to deferred revenue (contract liabilities). Finance reconciles deferred revenue monthly and provides balance roll-forward for audit.

Revenue exceptions and escalations
- Unusual arrangements (e.g., implementation bundle with significant customization or revenue share with partners) require pre-approval from Accounting leadership and Legal.
- Revenue recognition policy deviations should be documented and approved by the Controller.

5) Operational controls and ownership

Roles and responsibilities
- CFO: Final owner of budgeting and rev rec policy.
- Controller: Day-to-day owner of revenue recognition, deferred revenue reconciliations, and external reporting.
- FP&A: Owner of budgeting cadence, model consolidation, and rolling forecasts.
- Procurement lead: Owner of procurement policy, vendor classification and POs.
- GC / Legal: Contract templates, red-lines, and legal risk.
- Product / Sales owners: Provide commercial inputs, usage forecasts, and contract requirements.

Controls and audit readiness
- Monthly close checklist: Revenue cut-off checks, deferred revenue reconciliations, invoice-to-contract tie-outs.
- Quarterly internal review: Sampling of contracts to ensure correct revenue treatment.
- External audit: Provide contract rollforwards, booking journals, and explanations for any revenue cut-off exceptions.

6) Templates, checklists, and links
- Budget submission template: [link to planning system] (include one-line business case and headcount table).
- Contract request form: [Contract Request Jira/ServiceNow link].
- Vendor security questionnaire: [link to Security questionnaire form].
- Revenue recognition checklist: attach supporting schedules (revenue bridge, deferred revenue rollforward, contract mapping).

7) FAQs and common scenarios
- Q: How do we treat free trials?
  A: Free trials are not recognized as revenue. If converted to paid with prepayment, treat prepayment as deferred revenue.
- Q: How to account for committed capacity credits?
  A: Invoice per contract terms; recognize rev ratably unless consumption-based allocation is contractually required.
- Q: Can Sales negotiate Net 60?
  A: Standard is Net 30. Requests for >30 days require Finance approval and are evaluated for credit risk.

Contact & escalation
- Finance operations (billing & AR): billing-ops@redwood-inference.internal
- FP&A (budgeting): fpna@redwood-inference.internal
- Contracts & Legal: contracts@redwood-inference.internal
- Procurement: procurement@redwood-inference.internal

Appendix A: Example journal entries (high level)
- Invoice with prepayment: Dr Cash; Cr Deferred revenue. When earned: Dr Deferred revenue; Cr Revenue.
- Monthly usage billing: Dr AR; Cr Revenue.

Appendix B: Glossary (selected)
- ACV: Annual Contract Value.
- COGS: Cost of Goods Sold.
- PO: Purchase Order.
- MSA: Master Services Agreement.
- SOW: Statement of Work.

Revision history
- 2025-09-15: Initial draft prepared by Eleanor Park.
- 2025-11-02: Incorporated Legal feedback (indemnity and liability caps).
- 2026-01-12: Published with updated procurement thresholds and monthly forecast cadence.
